readings.title: The appliance that was hardly used
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Amber Energy Group lent meters to residents curious about electricity use. One family expected its rarely used electric oven to dominate the bill because its power rating was high. Their records showed that a smaller device running continuously also mattered. The adviser explained the difference between power at a moment and energy used over time. The family did not stop cooking. It first investigated whether the continuously running device needed its current setting. A measurement became useful when it was connected to duration and purpose, rather than treated as a single impressive number.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: A warm room and an open window
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: An office complained that its heating was expensive while staff regularly opened windows because one room became too warm. Managers first suggested reminding everyone to keep windows closed. A caretaker instead checked the controls and found that the room's thermostat was poorly positioned. After adjustment, temperatures became easier to manage. Staff still ventilated the room when needed. The investigation showed why a behaviour that looked wasteful could be a response to a faulty system. Asking what made people act that way led to a more useful change than simply repeating a rule.

readings.title: The bill after a cold winter
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A household installed loft insulation and expected the next winter's energy bill to fall sharply. The bill was almost unchanged, causing disappointment. An adviser asked about prices and weather before judging the result. Energy prices had risen and the winter had been colder, while the family had used fewer units than in the previous year. This did not provide a perfect measure of the insulation's effect, but it showed why money alone was an incomplete comparison. The family began keeping both usage figures and relevant context when assessing future changes.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: Choosing the first improvement
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A community hall received several energy-saving proposals, from new windows to reminders about unused lights. Its budget could not cover every suggestion. Volunteers listed expected benefits, costs and maintenance needs, then began with controls that reduced heating in empty rooms. They recorded results before considering larger work. The choice was not a claim that windows never mattered. It reflected the hall's present conditions and available money. A practical sequence allowed the committee to learn from one improvement while retaining funds for essential repairs. The most visible project was not automatically the most useful first step.

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

An electricity bill shows a total, but it does not always explain how that total was reached. Observing individual activities can make energy use easier to understand. The aim is not to make daily life uncomfortable. It is to find changes that save resources while meeting real needs.
translation.referenceAnswer: 电费账单显示一个总数，却并不总能解释这个总数是怎样产生的。观察单项活动可以帮助人们更好地理解能源使用情况。目的不是让日常生活变得不舒服，而是找到既节约资源又满足实际需求的改变。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Discuss the value and limits of monitoring household electricity use. Suggest how a family could choose a practical first step.
writing.sampleAnswer: Monitoring electricity use can help a family understand where its bill comes from. A small appliance running all day may use more energy over time than a powerful appliance used briefly. However, a meter reading alone does not say whether that use is unnecessary. Comfort, safety and genuine household needs must also be considered. I suggest beginning with a week of simple records and choosing one avoidable source of continuous use to investigate. The family should compare units as well as money, because prices may change. A practical first step is better than a long list of restrictions that nobody follows. The purpose is to use resources thoughtfully while keeping the home suitable for the people who live there.
